producer_checks.information_cutoff: 3 November 2026; historical sources include Deutsche Bundesbank (2024), IMF (2019), CESifo Working Paper 4135 (2013), German Historical Museum, the Nuremberg proceedings, and 2025 scholarly balance-sheet analysis.
producer_checks.research_depth: PT-BR ~53.8k characters / >7,000 words; EN ~46.5k characters / >6,000 words; 31 analytical sections in each edition, 3 reproducible historical financial charts, an explanatory balance-sheet table, a quantitative annual stock table, a causal flow and a geographical mechanism map.
producer_checks.source_check: Revised to address rejected v1 findings: added Deutsches Historisches Museum's 1932 petition chronology; replaced duplicated GHDI photographic citation for New Plan and bilateral clearing with IMF research; introduced financial time series from Burret, Feld and Köhler, table 4, with stocks, total debt and currency separately classified; differentiated 4% vs 5% coupon in sources; QA source-by-source review still required.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Three matching line charts in EN/PT-BR, fiscal 1938/39–1944/45, nominal billions Reichsmarks: Mefo bills outstanding [11.9,11.4,10.8,10.1,9.5,8.8,8.1], general government debt [53.2,73.5,102.6,153.3,208,284.9,387.9], notes and coins in circulation [11,15.2,18.3,23.8,29.8,38.7,73]. producer_checks.translation_parity: Both language editions have 31 H2 chapters, identical three chart datasets, financial periods and balances, parallel 1932 petition and revised clearing and source discussion.
producer_checks.methodology: Separate the 1923 Rentenmark from the 1934 MEFO bills; bills are credit instruments not legal tender; distinguish issued flows from outstanding stocks, physical currency from bank liabilities and fiscal debt, economic from legal responsibility; illustrative RM100 accounting table explicitly hypothetical.
